Answer: \(C + 3 \left(7 x + 2\right)^{3}\).

retry.feedback: The result of an indefinite integral is not a unique curve unless a condition determines the constant.

addmaths-0606-int-area-axis.description: Find crossings, distinguish signed integral from area and add regions on opposite sides of the axis.

sections.title: When does the definite integral equal an area?
sections.label: Above axis

blocks.html:
On an interval where the curve is above or on the x-axis, its integral is the area beneath it.

When \(f(x)\ge0\) for \(a\le x\le b\), the area is \(\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm dx\).

figure.alt: The whole region under a downward parabola from negative two to two lies above the axis.
figure.caption: The parabola \(y=4-x^2\) has matching halves either side of \(x=0\). For the shaded region, integrate one half and double it.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Find the appropriate endpoints and check the sign of the integrand in the interval.

Find the given vertical bounds or the intersections with the x-axis. Test a point inside the region. If it is above the axis throughout, its height above the axis gives the integrand.

blocks.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
blocks.prompt:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(- x - 3\right) \left(9 x + 45\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
blocks.hint: Find the limits and decide the sign of the graph between them. The definite integral gives the area when the curve lies above the horizontal axis.
blocks.solution:
Set \(\left(- x - 3\right) \left(9 x + 45\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

Answer: \(-5, -3\).

blocks.html: A graph with an x-intercept can still lie entirely above the axis on the requested interval.

blocks.title: Find a positive area under a linear graph
blocks.prompt: Find the area between \(y=2x+1\) and the x-axis for \(0\le x\le2\).
blocks.hint: The graph is positive all the way across the interval, so its integral gives the geometric area.

sections.intro: Find the limits and decide the sign of the graph between them. The definite integral gives the area when the curve lies above the horizontal axis.

sections.title: Why can the definite integral be negative?
sections.label: Below axis

blocks.html:
The integral counts a region below the axis with a negative sign. Its geometric area is positive.

When \(f(x)\le0\) throughout the interval, the strip height is \(0-f(x)\).

figure.alt: The portion of the upward parabola between its roots is below the horizontal axis.
figure.caption: For \(y=x^2-1\), the axis is the upper boundary of the shaded region. The height of a strip is \(1-x^2\).

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Negate the signed integral for a region that stays below the axis.

Sketch the axis above the curve. Find the positive height by subtracting the curve from the axis. Equivalently, take the opposite of the signed integral.

blocks.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
blocks.prompt:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(3 - 3 x\right) \left(6 - x\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
blocks.hint: The integral gives a negative value when the curve stays below the axis. Change its sign to obtain the positive geometric area.
blocks.solution:
Set \(\left(3 - 3 x\right) \left(6 - x\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

Answer: \(1, 6\).

blocks.html: State the area as a positive value.

blocks.title: Change the sign below the x-axis
blocks.prompt: Find the area between \(y=x-4\) and the x-axis for \(1\le x\le3\).
blocks.hint: The upper boundary is \(y=0\). The vertical height is \(0-(x-4)\).
blocks.solution: Use height \(4-x\). The area is \(\left[4x-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_1^3=\frac{15}{2}-\frac72=4\).

retry.feedback: A negative value is the signed integral of the curve. Take the positive region area.

sections.intro: The integral gives a negative value when the curve stays below the axis. Change its sign to obtain the positive geometric area.

sections.title: How do you add areas across an axis crossing?
sections.label: Sum of regions

blocks.html:
A crossing divides the region into pieces with different signs.

When \(f(x)\) crosses the axis at \(c\), work on \([a,c]\) and \([c,b]\) separately.

figure.alt: Two triangular regions meet where the line crosses the x-axis at one.
figure.caption: For \(y=x-1\), the first triangle has base 1 and height 1. The second has base 2 and height 2. Both areas are added.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Integrate separately on each side of the crossing, then add the geometric areas.

Determine the signs on the two intervals first. Find a positive area on each side and add them. The absolute value of the single signed integral gives the difference of the two areas.

blocks.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
blocks.prompt:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(4 - x\right) \left(9 x + 9\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
blocks.hint: Split at each crossing inside the limits. Calculate each signed integral and add their magnitudes to find the total area.
blocks.solution:
Set \(\left(4 - x\right) \left(9 x + 9\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

Answer: \(-1, 4\).

blocks.html: Taking the absolute value after adding signed parts can cancel area.

blocks.title: Add both areas instead of cancelling them
blocks.prompt: Find the total area between \(y=2x\) and the x-axis for \(-1\le x\le2\).
blocks.hint: Split at zero. Use height \(-2x\) on the negative side and \(2x\) on the positive side.
blocks.solution: The two areas are \([-x^2]_{-1}^0=1\) and \([x^2]_0^2=4\). Their sum is \(5\).

retry.feedback: The signed integral subtracts the region below the axis. The total area adds both positive magnitudes.

blocks.html: Sketch the crossings and label your split points before integrating.

sections.intro: Split at each crossing inside the limits. Calculate each signed integral and add their magnitudes to find the total area.

examples.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
examples.question:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(3 - x\right) \left(10 x + 20\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
solution: Set \(\left(3 - x\right) \left(10 x + 20\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

examples.title: Use symmetry for an area above the axis
examples.question: Find the area between \(y=4-x^2\) and the x-axis for \(-2\le x\le2\).
solution: The graph meets the axis at \(x=-2\) and \(x=2\), and stays above the axis between them.
The two halves are mirror images. The area is \(2\int_0^2(4-x^2)\,\mathrm dx\).
The primitive is \(4x-\frac{x^3}{3}\). Subtract the value zero at \(x=0\) from \(8-\frac83=\frac{16}3\) at \(x=2\).
Doubling gives an area of \(\frac{32}3\) square units.

examples.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
examples.question:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(1 - x\right) \left(- 9 x - 45\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
solution: Set \(\left(1 - x\right) \left(- 9 x - 45\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

examples.title: Find the geometric area of a region below the axis
examples.question: Find the area bounded by \(y=x^2-1\) and the x-axis for \(-1\le x\le1\).
solution: On the interval, \(y\le0\). A vertical strip has height \(0-(x^2-1)=1-x^2\).
The area is \(\left[x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{1}\).
The upper evaluation is \(\frac23\) and the lower evaluation is \(-\frac23\). Hence the area is \(\frac43\) square units.

examples.title: Separate geometric area from a signed integral
examples.question:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(- x - 3\right) \left(7 x + 35\right)\).

Find the x-values where the curve meets the x-axis.
solution: Set \(\left(- x - 3\right) \left(7 x + 35\right)\) equal to zero and use the two linear factors.

examples.title: Split the integral where the graph crosses the axis
examples.question: Find the total area between \(y=x-1\) and the x-axis from \(x=0\) to \(x=3\).
solution: The crossing is at \(x=1\). The curve is below the axis on \([0,1]\) and above it on \([1,3]\).
Use heights \(1-x\) and \(x-1\) on the two intervals. The corresponding integrals are \(\left[x-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1=\frac12\) and \(\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-x\right]_1^3=2\).
Add the two positive areas to obtain \(\frac52\) square units. The shaded triangles in the diagram give the same result.

Use \(- \frac{x^{3}}{3} + 9 x\) to evaluate the signed integral separately on each of the following bounds.

From \(-5\) to \(-3\), the signed integral is \(- \frac{44}{3}\) and the area is \(\frac{44}{3}\).

revision.body:
When does the definite integral equal an area?

On an interval where the curve is above or on the x-axis, its integral is the area beneath it.

Why can the definite integral be negative?

The integral counts a region below the axis with a negative sign. Its geometric area is positive.

How do you add areas across an axis crossing?

A crossing divides the region into pieces with different signs.

Quick worked example

A curve has equation \(y=\left(- x - 3\right) \left(5 x + 25\right)\).

Calculate the total area between the curve and the x-axis for \(-8\le x\le -3\).

Expand the curve equation to \(y=- 5 x^{2} - 40 x - 75\). One antiderivative is \(F(x)=- \frac{5 x^{3}}{3} - 20 x^{2} - 75 x\).

Use \(F(b)-F(a)\) on each part of the shaded interval. From left to right, the signed results are \(-90, \frac{20}{3}\).

Add the magnitudes. The total area is \(\frac{290}{3}\) square units.
revision.checks:
• A graph with an x-intercept can still lie entirely above the axis on the requested interval.
  • State the area as a positive value.
revision.examTip: Sketch the crossings and label your split points before integrating.

addmaths-0606-int-between-curves.description: Find intersections, choose the upper curve on each interval and add exact areas.

sections.title: Which points provide the limits?
sections.label: Intersections

blocks.html:
At an intersection the two graphs have equal y-values.

For \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=g(x)\), intersections satisfy \(f(x)=g(x)\).

figure.alt: The horizontal line intersects the parabola at negative two and two. The enclosed region is shaded.
figure.caption: The purple line \(y=4\) and the blue parabola \(y=x^2\) meet where \(x^2=4\). Their two intersections set the bounds of the shaded region.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Equate the expressions and solve every admissible root. Use the intersection x-values as limits.

Use the x-coordinates as bounds. Check which graphs lie above the other between these bounds. If the problem gives vertical boundaries, use those instead of searching for new ones.

blocks.title: Find the region enclosed by a line and a curve
blocks.prompt:
The two graphs have equations \(y=- 2 x - 2\) and \(y=- 4 x^{2} - 26 x - 2\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
blocks.hint: At an intersection two values of y match. Subtract one equation from the other, then solve the resulting equation for x.
blocks.solution:
Equate the two equations and solve \(- 4 x \left(x + 6\right)=0\).

Answer: \(-6, 0\).

blocks.html: Intercepts of one of the curves are not necessarily the intersections.

blocks.title: Find the region enclosed by a line and a curve
blocks.prompt:
The two graphs have equations \(y=- 6 x - 5\) and \(y=- 3 x^{2} + 9 x - 5\).

Find the total area enclosed by the graphs between \(x=0\) and \(x=5\).
blocks.hint: Think of the area as many thin vertical strips. Their height at each x is the upper function minus the lower function.
blocks.solution:
Choose the upper curve separately on each interval between intersections.

From \(0\) to \(5\), the signed integral of the second curve minus the first is \(\frac{125}{2}\), so the area is \(\frac{125}{2}\).

Answer: \(\frac{125}{2}\).

retry.feedback: Always subtract the lower curve from the upper curve for geometric area. The upper curve can change at an intersection.

sections.intro: At an intersection two values of y match. Subtract one equation from the other, then solve the resulting equation for x.

sections.title: What is the height of a thin vertical strip?
sections.label: Upper lower

blocks.html:
The strip height is upper y minus lower y.

The area is \(\int_a^b\bigl(y_{\mathrm{upper}}-y_{\mathrm{lower}}\bigr)\,\mathrm dx\) where their order is fixed.

figure.alt: A vertical strip between a line and a parabola shows their difference in height.
figure.caption: The purple line \(y=x\) is higher than the blue parabola \(y=x^2\) between \(0\) and \(1\). The red strip runs from the parabola up to the line.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Use an interior x-value to identify the upper function, then integrate the difference.

Evaluate both expressions at a convenient point between intersections. The larger value is the top of a vertical strip. Even if both values are negative, their difference in this order is non-negative.

blocks.title: Find the region enclosed by two curves
blocks.prompt:
The two graphs have equations \(y=x^{2} - 4 x - 8\) and \(y=8 x^{2} + 66 x + 160\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
blocks.hint: At an intersection two values of y match. Subtract one equation from the other, then solve the resulting equation for x.
blocks.solution:
Equate the two equations and solve \(7 \left(x + 4\right) \left(x + 6\right)=0\).

Answer: \(-6, -4\).

blocks.html: Which curve is upper depends on the interval.

blocks.title: Use a positive height at every x
blocks.prompt: Find the area between \(y=x+3\) and \(y=x^2\) for \(0\le x\le1\).
blocks.hint: On this interval \(x+3\) lies above \(x^2\). Use their difference in that order.
blocks.solution: The area is \(\left[\frac{x^2}{2}+3x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\frac12+3-\frac13=\frac{19}6\).

sections.intro: Think of the area as many thin vertical strips. Their height at each x is the upper function minus the lower function.

sections.title: How do you add regions if the graphs cross more than twice?
sections.label: Multiple regions

blocks.html:
Ordering can change at each intersection.

For adjacent crossings \(a,c,b\), calculate the areas on \([a,c]\) and \([c,b]\) and add them.

figure.alt: The line and cubic switch vertical order at the origin. The regions on both sides are shaded in different colours.
figure.caption: The purple line is \(y=x\) and the blue cubic is \(y=x^3\). The cubic sits above the line on \((-1,0)\). The line sits above the cubic on \((0,1)\).

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Split at every relevant crossing and integrate upper minus lower on each interval before summing.

Re-check which curve is higher after each crossing. You may need to swap the order of subtraction. A touch without a change of order keeps the same difference on both sides.

blocks.title: Find the region enclosed by a line and a curve
blocks.prompt:
The two graphs have equations \(y=8 - 5 x\) and \(y=8 x^{3} - 16 x^{2} - 45 x + 56\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
blocks.hint: At an intersection two values of y match. Subtract one equation from the other, then solve the resulting equation for x.
blocks.solution:
Equate the two equations and solve \(8 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)=0\).

Answer: \(-2, 1, 3\).

blocks.html: One signed integral over both regions can undercount the area.

blocks.title: Switch the strip order where the curves cross
blocks.prompt: Find the total area between \(y=x\) and \(y=x^2\) on \([0,2]\).
blocks.hint: Split at \(x=1\). The line is higher on \([0,1]\) and the parabola is higher on \([1,2]\).
blocks.solution:
The first area is \(\left[\frac{x^2}2-\frac{x^3}3\right]_0^1=\frac16\). The second is \(\left[\frac{x^3}3-\frac{x^2}2\right]_1^2=\frac56\).

The total is \(\frac16+\frac56=1\) square unit.

retry.feedback: That is the difference between the two enclosed regions. Add their positive areas.

blocks.html: An area may cross the x-axis and still be found from upper minus lower. Use the difference of the two graph values.

sections.intro: The upper curve can change at a crossing. Split the interval there and test which function is larger on each piece.

examples.title: Find the region enclosed by a line and a curve
examples.question:
The two graphs have equations \(y=-6\) and \(y=- x^{2} - 9 x - 24\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
solution: Equate the two equations and solve \(- \left(x + 3\right) \left(x + 6\right)=0\).

examples.title: Find both intersections before calculating the area
examples.question: Find the area enclosed by the line \(y=4\) and the parabola \(y=x^2\).
solution: Set \(x^2=4\). The intersections have x-coordinates \(-2\) and \(2\).
At \(x=0\), the line is higher. That order stays the same until the graphs meet again.
The area is \(\left[4x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^2=\frac{16}3-\left(-\frac{16}3\right)=\frac{32}3\) square units.

examples.title: Find the region enclosed by two curves
examples.question:
The two graphs have equations \(y=x^{2} - 5 x + 8\) and \(y=7 x^{2} - 5 x - 46\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
solution: Equate the two equations and solve \(6 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)=0\).

examples.title: Translate the upper and lower graphs into a strip height
examples.question: Find the area enclosed by \(y=x\) and \(y=x^2\).
solution: At an intersection \(x=x^2\). Factoring \(x(x-1)=0\) gives the limits \(0\) and \(1\).
Between these limits, squaring a number between zero and one makes it smaller. The strip height is \(x-x^2\).
Integrating gives \(\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\frac12-\frac13=\frac16\) square units.

examples.title: Find the region enclosed by a line and a curve
examples.question:
The two graphs have equations \(y=5 x + 1\) and \(y=2 x^{3} - 16 x^{2} + 23 x + 37\).

Find the x-coordinates of all intersections.
solution: Equate the two equations and solve \(2 \left(x - 6\right) \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 1\right)=0\).

examples.title: Add two regions with opposite vertical order
examples.question: Find the total area between \(y=x\) and \(y=x^3\) for \(-1\le x\le1\).
solution: Solving \(x^3=x\) gives crossings at \(-1,0,1\). In the left half \(x^3>x\), while in the right half \(x>x^3\).
The two regions have equal areas by rotational symmetry about the origin. The right-hand region has area \(\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^1=\frac14\).
Doubling gives \(\frac12\) square units. A single signed integral of \(x-x^3\) would cancel the two regions.

extraPractice.title: Find the region enclosed by two curves

extraPractice.solution:
Equate the two equations and solve \(10 x \left(x - 2\right)=0\).

Answer: \(0, 2\).

extraPractice.title: Find the region enclosed by two curves
extraPractice.prompt:
The two graphs have equations \(y=x^{2} + 2 x - 4\) and \(y=11 x^{2} + 42 x - 54\).

Find the total area enclosed by the graphs between \(x=-5\) and \(x=1\).
extraPractice.hint: Think of the area as many thin vertical strips. Their height at each x is the upper function minus the lower function.
extraPractice.solution:
Choose the upper curve separately on each interval between intersections.

From \(-5\) to \(1\), the signed integral of the second curve minus the first is \(-360\), so the area is \(360\).

revision.body:
Which points provide the limits?

At an intersection the two graphs have equal y-values.

What is the height of a thin vertical strip?

The strip height is upper y minus lower y.

How do you add regions if the graphs cross more than twice?

Ordering can change at each intersection.

Quick worked example

The two graphs have equations \(y=- 5 x - 1\) and \(y=- 8 x^{2} + 19 x - 1\).

Find the total area enclosed by the graphs between \(x=0\) and \(x=3\).

Subtract the second equation from the first. The difference is \(8 x^{2} - 24 x\).

Split at the intersections inside the stated limits. An antiderivative of the difference is \(\frac{8 x^{3}}{3} - 12 x^{2}\).

Evaluate upper endpoint minus lower endpoint on each part. The signed results are \(-36\).

Add their magnitudes to get \(36\) square units.
revision.checks:
• Intercepts of one of the curves are not necessarily the intersections.
  • Which curve is upper depends on the interval.
revision.examTip: An area may cross the x-axis and still be found from upper minus lower. Use the difference of the two graph values.
